title: Baked mac and cheese
subtitle: Southern soul food baked macaroni and cheese
excerpt: Elbow macaroni in a rich egg-and-cheese custard, layered with extra cheese and baked until set with a golden, slightly crisp crust. The Southern American approach to baked mac and cheese: denser, richer, and more substantial than the stove-top version.
sourceNotes: Baked macaroni and cheese has deep roots in American cooking, with early versions appearing in Mary Randolph's The Virginia Housewife (1824, public domain) and Thomas Jefferson's Monticello table. The Southern soul food version, with an egg-and-cream custard rather than a béchamel, is documented in African-American cooking texts including Edna Lewis's The Taste of Country Cooking (1976) and Leah Chase's The Dooky Chase Cookbook (1990).

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely and freeze in the dish. Defrost overnight in the fridge, cover with foil, and bake at 160°C for 20 minutes to heat through, uncovering for the last 5 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be assembled the day before and refrigerated. Add 10 minutes to the baking time.

content.text: Southern baked mac and cheese is not the same thing as mac and cheese from a box. It is a proper custard-based bake: eggs, evaporated milk, and a generous amount of cheddar set around the cooked pasta and baked until the whole thing is firm, sliceable, and golden. It feeds a crowd, holds well, and is the kind of side dish that people eat three portions of without noticing.

items.prepNote: freshly grated; divided: 400 g in the custard, 200 g on top

content.text: Cook the macaroni in well-salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet time (it will continue cooking in the oven). Drain well.

Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C). Whisk the eggs, evaporated milk, whole milk, mustard powder, cayenne, salt, and pepper together in a large bowl. Add 400 g of the grated cheese and stir to combine. Add the hot drained macaroni and the butter cubes and stir everything together.
Pour into a buttered baking dish. Scatter the remaining 200 g of cheese evenly over the top.

Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is golden and the custard is just set. It should wobble slightly in the centre when you shake the dish; it will set more as it rests. Leave to rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.cause: Oven too hot, or baked for too long
items.fix: Southern baked mac needs no higher than 180°C. A slight wobble in the centre when you remove it from the oven is correct; it will firm up on standing.

items.cause: Cooked too long before baking, or baked too long
items.fix: Under-cook the pasta by 2 minutes before it goes into the custard. It continues to cook in the oven.

content.text: Baked mac and cheese is a foundational dish of Southern American and African-American cooking. It appears at Thanksgiving and Christmas alongside turkey and sweet potato casserole. It is a fixture at church suppers and family reunions across the South. The egg-custard version is distinct from the Northern béchamel version and from the box version. It is richer, denser, and cut into squares rather than ladled from a pan.
